title: Select All Sewn Patterns (ver. 12.2)
content: ### Objective Makes it easier to select multiple pattern pieces that are connected by sewing relationships. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move tool ▶ Double-click on a pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern tool ▶ Double-click on a pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern tool (right-click on Pattern) ▶ "Select All Sewn (Ctrl + Alt + A)" Main Menu Toolbar ▶ Edit ▶ "Select All Sewn (Ctrl + Alt + A)" ### Operation 1. Follow the dedicated path for the tool found in "Location" above. 2. All patterns that are either directly or indirectly linked by sewing relationships will be selected. ※ Note: \- Select multiple patterns using Shift key. While holding down Shift key, double-click on a specific pattern or use right-click to open the drop-down menu on a pattern piece and pick "Select All Sewn Patterns" to select additional pattern pieces with sewing relationship while maintaining the pre-existing selection. -Piping, binding, buttons, interior shapes, and sewn objects are not selected with the Select All Sewn Patterns feature. -Patterns connected by zippers are selected together with the "Select All Sewn Patterns" feature. -At least 1 pattern piece must be selected for the hotkeys to work.
content_description: This web page provides an efficient guide for selecting multiple interconnected pattern pieces in sewing software using various tools and commands.

title: Symmetrical 3D State (ver. 2024.0)
content: Easily apply the simulation of pattern to its symmetric pattern. ### Steps 1\. This feature only applies to patterns with Symmetrized set. 2\. In the 3D window, right-click on a pattern that is set to symmetrically. 3\. Select the Symmetric Arrangement menu from the right-click pop-up menu. ### End Result The selected pattern is transformed into a simulated version of the opposite Symmetric pattern and is symmetrically arranged relative to the origin of the grid.
content_description: This webpage provides a simple guide to simulating and symmetrically arranging patterns using the Symmetric Arrangement feature in the 3D window.

title: Omniverse Connector
content: ## [![940x90-2.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438579593369)](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/omniverse/) ### Location Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ Onmiverse Connector (ver. 2025.0) Side Panel Title Bar ▶ Right-click Dropdown menu Onmiverse Connector (ver. 2025.0) ## ## Feature Overview Through data exchange with the Omniverse platform using USD, collaboration workflows can be accelerated. The following steps are required to use the Omniverse Connector. For more information on NVIDIA and Omniverse, please check out the links below. 1. Create NVIDIA account ([link](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/omniverse/)) 2. Download and install the Omniverse Launcher ([link](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/omniverse/download/)) 3. Set the Omniverse server ([link](https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/prod_nucleus/prod_nucleus/overview.html)) Once done setting up your server in Omniverse Launcher, you can either add the server(Add Server) or join the session(Join Session) in Marvelous Designer. ## Add Server You can add Omniverse Nucleus server in Marvelous Designer. ### Steps Follow the indicated guideline below. Location ![omniverse_server.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438590876441) Marvelous Designer ▶ Omniverse Connector Window ▶ Click on the Omniverse icon ▶ Add Server Enter the server address in the Omniverse Server Connector, and then click on the Add Server button. ### End Result Now you are successfully connected to the server that you entered. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438580043161) ## Create Session / Join Session Create a session for USD files in Omniverse USD Composer, and then you can join that session in Marvelous Designer. ### Step 1. Open a USD file After done connecting to the server, open a USD file which from both Omniverse USD Composer and Marvelous Designer to connect to the session. **Location** **Open a USD file in Marvelous Designer** Marvelous Designer ▶ Omniverse Connector Window ▶ Double-click the Designated Folder \- The files within the folder are displayed in the file list below. \- Double-click or drag & drop the desired file to open it. Also, you can click the right mouse button on the desired file to select Open. **Open a USD file in Omniverse USD Composer** Omniverse USD Composer ▶ Content Tab ▶ Select the Desired Folder ▶ Open the Same File Opened in Marvelous Designer #### End Result The file you opened will be shown in both the 2D and the 3D window, and the list of layers from the file is also displayed in the USD Layer window. ### Step 2. Create Session in Omniverse USD Composer Once you open a USD file, you can create a session in Omniverse USD Composer. * Please Note. Create Session is not available in Marvelous Designer. Location ![omniverse_session_create.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438591178265) Omniverse USD Composer ▶ LIVE Icon Submenu ▶ Create Session \- Enter a session name to create a new session. #### End Result ![session_live_authoring.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438580296473) A session is succesfully created, and you are automatically joined that session with the LIVE icon is activated in Omniverse USD Composer. The Live Session Layer is displayed once you are joined the session. ### Steps 3. Join Session in Marvelous Designer After creating a session in Omniverse USD Composer, you can join the session in Marvelous Designer. **Location** ![marvelous_session_join.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438580550297) Marvelous Designer ▶ Omniverse Connector Window ▶ Click the Omniverse Icon ▶ Join Session \- Select the desired session from the Join Live Session drop-down menu, and click on the Join button. #### End Result Once you are joined the session, the layer from the session is added as a Live type in the USD Layer window. The layer will have the same name as the Live Session Layer in Omniverse USD Composer, and be set to the Authoring Layer. ![session_live_authoring2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438591739033) ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438580043161) **Live Indicator** When joining a session, you can find the live indicator in both Marvelous Designer and Omniverse USD Composer. ![omniverse_live.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438581083417) Marvelous Designer ▶ Omniverse Connector Window ▶ The Live indicator appears on the Omniverse icon **Session Participants (in Marvelous Designer)** ![omniverse_session_member_.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438592147481) Marvelous Designer ▶ Omniverse Connector Window ▶ Click on the Refresh Participants button right next to the Server. The session participants icon appears on the left of the Omniverse icon. Hover your mouse on the icon to see the participants and their software information. **Session Participants (in Omniverse USD Composer)** ![omniverse_session_member2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438592384153) Omniverse USD Composer ▶ The name of the participant appears on the right of the Live icon The session participants icon appears next to the Live icon. Hover your mouse on the icon to see the participants and their software information. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438580043161) ## Session in Progress ### Export files from Marvelous Designer to Omniverse USD Composer When a session in Omniverse USD Composer is connected in Marvelous Designer, you can export your work in Marvelous Designer to Omniverse USD Composer through the Export to USD Layer feature. The way Omniverse USD Composer updates the work depends on the type of USD layer (USD, LIVE) that the Authoring Layer is set to. ### Steps ### Where the Live Session Layer is set as the Authoring Layer ![usd_live_authoring.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438581715097) Select desired clothing or trims and click on Export to USD Layer from the right mouse button pop-up menu. #### End Result \- The changes of the session layer is directly reflected to the Omniverse USD Composer. \- If there is no Prim with the same name on the same Prim Path in Omniverse USD Composer, add a new Prim (Append). \- If there is a Prim with the same name in the Prim Path you set for export in Omniverse USD Composer, the changes will be overwritten on that Prim. ### Where a USD Layer is set as the Authoring Layer ![usd_usd_authoring.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438592802457) Select desired clothing or trims and click on Export to USD Layer from the right mouse button pop-up menu. #### End Result \- The selected are exported to the USD file, but not directly reflected to the Omniverse USD Composer. \- To see these changes in the Omniverse USD Composer, click the FETCH button when the 'Base USD files have been changed' pop-up appears. ![usd_fetch.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438582081689) \- If there is no Prim with the same name on the same Prim Path in Omniverse USD Composer, add a new Prim (Append). \- If there is a Prim with the same name in the Prim Path you set for export in Omniverse USD Composer, the changes will be overwritten on that Prim. ### * How to update the changes from Omniverse USD Composer to Marvelous Designer Marvelous Designer cannot directly reflect any changes from Omniverse USD Composer. If you need to use a USD file which is modified from the Omniverse USD Composer, the file should be reimported to Marvelous Designer. Merge the USD changes Omniverse USD Composer, and then reimport the file in Marvelous Designer. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438580043161) ## Leave Session You can leave the session that you're in both Marvelous Designer and Omniverse USD Composer. ### Steps #### Leave Session in Marvelous Designer Location ![omniverse_leave2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438582359065) Marvelous Designer ▶ Omniverse Connector Window ▶ Click the Omniverse Icon ▶ Leave Session \- Click on the Leave button when Information pop-up window appears. #### End Result The current session ends and the Live mark disappears from the Omniverse icon. The list of session participants disappears. #### Leave Session in Omniverse USD Composer Location ![omniverse_leave.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438626917273) Omniverse USD Composer ▶ Live Icon Submenu ▶ Leave Session \- Click on the Leave button in the Leave Session window. #### End Result The current session ends and the Live status is changed to deactivated. The list of session participants disappears. * Please try out this **[USD sample file](https://s3.marvelousdesigner.com/newmdweb/helpcenter/manual/KoiFish_USD.zip) **we created with Marvelous Designer and see how the new USD support can benefit your workflow. You can find step by step **[tutorial](https://youtu.be/r7AfPVd8WG4)** for how to export this USD file from Marvelous Designer.
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide on utilizing the Omniverse Connector in Marvelous Designer to enhance collaborative workflows through seamless USD data exchange.

title: ANIMATION MODE: Record Animation
content: ### Objective Record garment animation. ※ Note: Follow the link; [Process of Making Garment Animation](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000560428) for your reference on creating garment animation in details. ### Location Animation Mode ▶ Animation Editor ▶ Record ### Operation 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Animation Mode ▶ Animation Editor ▶ Record → Simulation turns on automatically and it is now being recorded in frames. → If a Transition Animation is created, the recording automatically stops at the end of the Transition Animation frame and starts again (ver2.5.0). ※ Note: Transition Animation is auto-generated animation tool which automatically generates for stabilizing transition when the original Avatar pose is different to the first pose in the motion file. Once the garment and avatar arrive in a new position, it is no longer in need therefore the recording automatically stops for you to delete this unnecessary part. The Transition Animation for default avatars of version10 is not compatible with the previous versions. 2\. Once the Avatar's motion ends, the recording automatically stops. To stop the recording while it is in process, click the Pause button. **Copy Frame** The feature is to create assets for Dynamic Wrinkle. (ver. 5.1.445) \- After recording an animation of a garment and copy /paste on designated frame.
content_description: This web page serves as a guide for users to effectively record garment animations using the Animation Editor in CLO 3D, complete with operational steps and tips for managing transitions.

title: Transform Point/Segment
content: ### ### ### ### ### Objective Transform a Pattern by scaling or rotating its point and segment. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Point/Segment 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern tool (hold down the button)▶ Transform Point/Segment ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Point/Segment 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern tool (hold down the button)▶ Transform Point/Segment 2. Select the point/segment to be transformed. → The selected point/segment is highlighted in yellow and the surrounding marquee box appears. → The Transform pattern tool's selection box can now select patterns no matter the area it covers; by holding CTRL and clicking and dragging your mouse. (ver. 2024.0) 3. Move, scale, or rotate the selected point/segment. → The Pattern is transformed as the selected points/segments are edited.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for transforming a pattern by scaling or rotating its points and segments using the Edit Pattern tool.

title: Complete Nonlinear Simulation
content: ### Objective This function allows more accurate Simulation on fabric stretch (ver3.0.0). It is especially effective for longer Garments. ※ Note: This is available from ver3.0.0 onward. ### Location 3D Garment Window ▶ Right-click Pop-up Menu ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ Property Editor ▶ Nonlinear Simulation ### Operation Follow the indicated guideline below and check the Nonlinear Simulation On: 3D Garment Window ▶ Simulation Property Editor ▶ Preset ▶ Complete (Nonlinear) → Fabric strength and elongation are now being simulated more accurately.
content_description: This webpage provides guidance on utilizing the enhanced Nonlinear Simulation feature in version 3.0.0 for more precise fabric stretch modeling, particularly for longer garments.

title: Flip Normal
content: ### Objective Easily flip the wrong/right side of Fabric before or after draping. Sew Patterns as desired first and flip the fabric surface at last to save time. ### Location Garment Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Pattern ▶ Flip Normal ### Operation 1. Select Select/Move tool. 2. Select a Pattern to flip. 3. Follow the indicated guideline below: Garment Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Pattern ▶ Flip Normal → The selected pattern's fabric surface is now being flipped over. ※ Note: Fold Angle value also gets flipped when flipping normal (ver2.4.0).
content_description: "Quickly and efficiently flip the fabric surface of your patterns in Fabric before or after draping to streamline your sewing process."

title: 2D Pattern View Controls
content: ### Objective #### Zoom to Selected Zoom in to the selected Pattern at your convenience. #### Zoom Extents All Zoom in or out the 2D window to see all Patterns. #### Smart Panning The 2D window is going to pan automatically following the mouse cursor. ### Location #### Zoom to Selected Display ▶ Viewpoint ▶ Focus Zoom Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ Zoom to Selected Click (on Pattern) ▶ F key on the keyboard #### Zoom Extents All Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D window) ▶ Zoom Extents All #### Smart Panning Main Menu ▶ Applicable Select/Edit Tool 3D/ 2D Toolbar ▶ Applicable Select/Edit Tool ※ Note: #### Applicable Select/Edit Tool: Tools used to create pattern/internal shapes, create/edit sewing lines, and create/edit topstitches have smart panning function. ### Operation #### Zoom to Selected 1. Navigate to the 2D Toolbar and select the Transform Pattern or the Edit Pattern. 2. Left click on the pattern to be zoomed in. 3. Follow the indicated guideline below: Display ▶ Viewpoint ▶ Focus Zoom Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ Zoom to Selected Left Click (on Pattern) ▶ F key on the keyboard →The 2D window is scaled to the selected pattern and the 2D window can be controlled on the basis of the selected Pattern. #### Zoom Extents All 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D window) ▶ Zoom Extents All → The 2D window is scaled to show all Patterns in the 2D window. #### Smart Panning 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Applicable Select/Edit Tool 3D/ 2D Toolbar ▶ Applicable Select/Edit Tool →The 2D Window is going to pan automatically following the mouse cursor.
content_description: This web page provides essential instructions for effectively zooming and panning within a 2D workspace to enhance your pattern editing experience.

title: Other (Above ver4.2.0)
content: ### Objective Change the default settings of the software in User Settings. Designated settings will become the default after the program is restarted. Shortcut keys, menus, graphics options, view controls, default files, font settings, and other miscellaneous properties can be set in User Settings. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ Others Main Menu ▶ Settings/Preferences ▶ Preferences ▶ Others (ver 11) ### Operation 1. Adjust the settings below as needed: MetaData | Show Option to Save MetaData | Turn on the 'Show Option to Save MetaData', the options appears when saving your project or garment and metadata file together is shown again. ---|---|--- Modular Configurator | Maintain Block Selections with Same Name | In Modular Mode, pattern selection is maintained when Blocks have the same name. Maintain Fabric Properties for Patterns with Same Name | In Modular Mode, fabric application is maintained when Blocks have the same name.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on customizing default software settings in User Settings, allowing users to tailor shortcut keys, menus, graphics options, and more for an optimized experience.

title: Slash & Spread
content: ### ### ### ### Objective Slash and spread a Pattern using an Internal Line inside the Pattern (ver2.4.0). ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Slash & Spread 2D Toolbar ▶ Slash & Spread ### Operation #### Slash & Spread 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Slash & Spread 2D Toolbar ▶ Slash & Spread 2. Click on the Pattern outline to draw a Slash Line. Drag the mouse as the Slash Line follows along the mouse cursor. Click again on the Pattern outline to complete the Slash Line. Or, Click on the Internal Line within the Pattern to set it as a Slash Line (ver2.5.0). 3. Choose the side of the Pattern to be rotated. → The selected side of the Pattern is highlighted in yellow. 4. Drag the mouse cursor towards the Pattern should be rotated. → The preview of the edited pattern appears. 5. When the desired shape is achieved, click on the 2D window to complete Slash & Spread. #### Slash & Spread with Distance and Angle 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Slash & Spread 2D Toolbar ▶ Slash & Spread 2. Click on the Pattern outline to draw a Slash Line. Drag the mouse as the Slash Line follows along the mouse cursor. Click again on the Pattern outline to complete the Slash Line. Or, click on the Internal Line within the Pattern to set it as a Slash Line (ver2.5.0). 3. Right click on the 2D window to access the pop-up menu. → The Spread window appears. 4. Enter the desired values for Distance and Angle. Distance | Set how much in length the selected side of the Pattern spreads. ---|--- Angle | Set the angle the selected side of the Pattern spreads. 5. Click OK to complete Slash & Spread. ※ Note: * When selecting an Internal Line as a Slash Line, the side closer to the mouse cursor spreads. * Click on the slash line to spread patterns on both sides. (ver MD10) * The shape of the Pattern can be previewed when closing the Pattern. Also, the Pattern Outline is smoothened into a natural curve. (ver MD10)
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for using the Slash & Spread feature in version 2.4.0 to manipulate 2D patterns by creating and adjusting Slash Lines.

title: 2D (Above ver4.2.0)
content: ### Objective Change the default settings of the software in User Settings. Designated settings will become the default after the program is restarted. Shortcut keys, menus, graphics options, view controls, default files, font settings, and other miscellaneous properties can be set in User Settings. In the 2D section, configure settings related to 2D features. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ 2D Main Menu ▶ Settings/Preferences ▶ Preferences ▶ 2D (ver 11) ### Operation 1. Adjust the settings below as needed: Pattern | Default Particle Distance | Set the default particle distance when creating patterns. ---|---|--- Automatically Offset 2D Patterns when Cut | Toggle the option to offset 2D patterns when the Cut function is used, making it easier to work with UV export (ver3.2.0).
content_description: This web page provides guidance on how to customize the default settings for 2D features in the software, ensuring improved user experience and functionality.

title: Button Right-Click Menus
content: ### Objective Change status of buttons as desired. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button ▶ Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D/2D Button) Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D/2D Button) ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button ▶ Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D/2D Button) Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D/2D Button) 2. Right-click on the button to edit. → Button related pop-up menu appears. Pop-up Menu | Description ---|--- Reset 3D Position | Reset to location of pre-simulation. Copy | Copy the selected button. Paste | Paste the selected button. Mirror Paste (Position Only) | Mirror paste the position of the selected button. Delete | Delete the selected button. Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern | Duplicate the selected button to its symmetric pattern. Activate/Deactivate | Activate or deactivate the selected button. Freeze/Unfreeze | Freeze or unfreeze the selected button. Set Number of Sewing Layers | Set the number of sewing layers for the selected button. After setting the Number of Sewing Layers, use the Select/Move Button tool to adjust buttons' locations on each Patterns. Flip | Move the selected button to the opposite side. Align | Align selected buttons based on the selected options. Distribute | Distribute selected buttons horizontally or vertically with same intervals
content_description: This web page provides comprehensive instructions for modifying the status and arrangement of buttons within the 3D Toolbar and Main Menu, enhancing user control over button functionalities.

title: Circumference Avatar Tape  (ver. 5.1.4)
content: ### Related articles [Linear Avatar Tape](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358281835673) [Attach to Avatar Tape](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358293301145) [Delete Avatar Tape](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358298422553) ### ### Objective Create a circumference baseline on avatars to improve accuracy in fit and draping. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Tape ▶ Circumference Avatar Tape 3D Toolbar ▶ Circumference Avatar Tape ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Tape ▶ Circumference Avatar Tape 3D Toolbar ▶ Circumference Avatar Tape 2. Click to make the beginning point of the tape at a desired place. → Blue dot appears and gets fixed. 3. Click another place to make the second point. → Another blue dot appears and gets fixed and a connected line between both of the dots appears. 4. Click to complete.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating a circumference baseline on avatars to enhance fit and draping accuracy in your designs.

title: MODULAR MODE: Edit Blocks
content: ### Objective Open and edit Patterns in provided Blocks from the Modular Configurator or replace them with your own. ### Location Modular Mode ▶ Block Editor ### Operation Edit Patterns 1\. Load Blocks from the Modular Configurator. 2\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶ Block Editor 3\. Select a Block to edit in the list of the Block Editor. → Remaining Blocks are frozen. 4\. Modify it with the Edit Pattern tool. 5\. Once the modification is done, Simulate the according Block when the rest of the Blocks are still frozen. 6\. Once the modification is completed, reselect the selected Block. → All of the Blocks are activated again. Replace Patterns 1.Load Blocks from the Modular Configurator. 2\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶ Block Editor 3\. Locate Patterns out of Block Boxes or delete them. → The Block Boxes remain in light grey. 4\. Add desired Garment files to substitute with. 5.Click and drag the Patterns that are just loaded to matching Block Boxes. → The Patterns are linked with the Block Boxes. 6\. Sew the Patterns to Block Boxes. 7\. Select the according Block in the Block Editor, freeze the rest, then Simulate. ※ Note: * Selected Blocks in the Block Editor are also selected in the 2D window. * Editing Pattern in the Modular Mode is the same as the Simulation Mode. Deleting a segment or a point in a Pattern also deletes Sewing Lines between the Pattern and the Block Box.
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for users to open, edit, or replace patterns within blocks using the Modular Configurator's Block Editor.

title: 3D Free Sewing (VER4.2.0)
content: ### Objective In the 3D window, freely establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes/Lines. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Free Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ Free Sewing ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Free Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ Free Sewing → All sew-able segments are bolded. → All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. 2. Click, drag and double click on Pattern outline or Internal Shape/Line to establish the start and end points of the first half of the seam. 3. Similarly, click again on another Pattern outline or Internal Shape/Line to establish the start point of the second half of the seam. → Drag the mouse cursor as a blue point appears guiding the length of the first half of the seam. 4. The mouse cursor snaps to the blue guide point. 5. Be mindful to make the Directional Notches parallel to each other and click to complete the second half of the seam. ※ Note: * The face of the Directional Notch of a Sewing Line defers depending on the order of establishing the start and the end point of the Sewing Line. * Right click while establishing the Free Sewing Line to enter the desired length of the Sewing Line in the Create Sewing Line window. * Use the shortcut to establish M:N sewing lines. For more detail, please reference M:N Free Sewing. ※ Note: 3D Sewing Video
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide for users to create and manipulate Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes in both 2D and 3D environments.

title: Remeshing to Retopology (Selected)  (ver. 5.1.4)
content: ### Objective Remesh selected pattern and generate retopology lines along the remeshed polygon. ### Location Right-click pattern pop-up menu (3D window) → Remeshing to Retopology ### Operation 1. Click the menu specified in Location. 2. A polygon count input dialog will pop up. → Enter the desired number of polygons and click the Apply button. 3. The mesh of the selected patterns is rearranged into an aligned quad mesh. 4. Retopology lines are generated along the remeshed polygons. 5. To return to the previous status, right-click on the pattern and select 'Undo Remeshing' from the pop-up menu.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for using the Remesh feature to create aligned quad meshes and generate retopology lines for selected patterns in a 3D modeling environment.

title: Fabric List Window
content: Default_Fabric is provided as default Fabric, and being displayed in the Fabric list. When editing Default_Fabric, the edited default Fabric maintains until reopen a garment or rerun a program. You can reset edited properties of Default_Fabric with > Right Click > Pop Up Menu.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide guidance on managing and resetting Default_Fabric settings within the Fabric list, ensuring users can effectively edit and maintain their fabric properties.

title: Delete Avatar
content: ### Objective Select avatar and delete individually. ※ Note: Versions below ver2.5.0 only allow avatar deletion for all. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Delete Avatar 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Pop-up Menu (Right-click on Avatar) ▶ Delete Avatar ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Delete Avatar 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Pop-up Menu (Right-click on Avatar) ▶ Delete Avatar → The avatar is now being deleted. ※ Note: From ver2.5.0, deleted avatars can immediately be restored at Main Menu ▶ Edit ▶ Undo or Press (Ctrl+Z)
content_description: This web page provides instructions for selecting and individually deleting avatars in the application, while noting version-specific limitations and restoration options.

title: AVATAR CREATING MEASUREMENT: Height Measurement
content: ### Objective Take avatar's height measurements from the ground to the relevant points. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Measurement ▶ Height Measurement Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D window Toolbar) ▶ Measurement Toolbar ▶ (Hold left mouse button at least two seconds) ▶ Height Measurement ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Measurement ▶ Height Measurement Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D window Toolbar) ▶ Measurement Toolbar ▶ (Hold left mouse button at least two seconds) ▶ Height Measurement 2. Click a point to take the height measurement. 3. Double-click another point to end the height measurement. → A light-green colored rectangle indicating the ground automatically appears, and a green line connecting the ground and the clicked point appears to indicate the height.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for accurately measuring an avatar's height from the ground to specific points using the measurement tools in the 3D interface.

title: BUTTON STYLE PROPERTIES: Button Size
content: ### Objective Adjust button sizes as desired. ### Location #### Before ver4.0.0 Object Browser ▶ Button Tab ▶ Property Editor ▶ Size #### After ver4.0.0 Object Browser ▶ Button Tab ▶ Property Editor ▶ Width/ Thickness/ Weight ### Operation #### Before ver4.0.0 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Select a button item in the Button Tab. → Its properties appear in the Property Editor. 2. Find the Size option and enter desired value. → The button size is now being adjusted and applied. #### After ver4.0.0 1. Navigate to the Object Browser and select the desired Button item from the button tab. → The selected button item's properties appear in the Property Editor. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Button Tab ▶ Property Editor ▶ Width/ Thickness/ Weight 3. Refer to the table below and adjust each option as needed. Option | Description ---|--- Width | Adjust button width. Thickness | Enter the desired value for button thickness. Weight | Enter the desired value for button weight in grams.
content_description: This webpage serves as a guide for adjusting button sizes in the Object Browser, detailing the steps and options available before and after version 4.0.0.

title: Delete All Overlapping Points
content: ### Objective Delete overlapping points on patterns/internal shapes (ver2.5.0). When cutting Patterns in Marvelous Designer, two Segment Points can be created very close to each other, below the minimum distance set by Marvelous Designer. When the aforementioned case happens, the respective Patterns cannot be moved nor edited, but can be resolved by deleting the overlapping points. ### Location Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) ▶ Delete All Overlapping Points ### Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) ▶ Delete All Overlapping Points → All overlapping points on Patterns and Internal Shapes are deleted.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for using the "Delete All Overlapping Points" feature in Marvelous Designer to resolve issues with overlapping segment points in patterns and internal shapes.

title: Duplicate as Button to Symmetric Pattern
content: ### Objective Duplicate buttons as buttonholes, or buttonholes as buttons, to its Symmetric Pattern. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button 2. Click on the button or buttonhole to be duplicated to its Symmetric Pattern. → The selected button or buttonhole is highlighted in yellow. 3. Right click on the selected button or buttonhole. → The right-click pop-up menu appears. 4. Depending on the selected item, select Duplicate as Button to Symmetric Pattern or Duplicate as Buttonhole to Symmetric Pattern. → The selected button or buttonhole is duplicated as a buttonhole or button, depending on the selected item, to its Symmetric Pattern.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for duplicating buttons and buttonholes to their Symmetric Pattern in a 3D design environment.

title: Layer Clone
content: ### Objective Create an instance of the Pattern in its 3D state while sewing its Pattern outlines and Internal Lines to its instance's Pattern outlines and Internal Lines. Use the function to easily create padded jackets, collars, cuffs and other garments/details made with multiple layers of Patterns. ### Location Right Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Layer Clone (Over/Under) ### Operation 1. Select Transform Pattern tool or Edit Pattern tool. 2. Select the Patterns to be layer cloned. 3. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Layer Clone (Over) → The cloned Pattern is placed above the original Pattern. Right Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Layer Clone (Under) → The cloned Pattern is placed beneath the original Pattern. 4. Activate Simulation. → The cloned layer is simulated based on the option selected.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for utilizing the Layer Clone function to efficiently create 3D instances of garment patterns, enhancing the design of padded jackets, collars, cuffs, and other layered details.

title: Copy Buttonhole Style
content: ### Objective Copy and modify a buttonhole in order to create a new buttonhole style or adjust its properties. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab ▶ Copy ### Operation 1. Navigate to the Object Browser and select an item in the buttonhole tab. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab ▶ Copy → A new buttonhole item with the same properties of the selected item is now being created.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for copying and modifying buttonholes to create new styles or adjust their properties.

title: ADD CUSTOM BUTTON AND BUTTONHOLE: Register Custom OBJ as Button
content: ### Objective Register a custom OBJ file as Button. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Register Button Property Editor ▶ Shape ▶ plus_button.png ### Operation #### #### Create Button OBJ Please check below requirements before registering an OBJ as a button. ※Required: * Position the face of an OBJ towards Y-axis. * Position the contact point of an OBJ where it should be attached to 3D garments at 0,0,0 (x,y,z) coordinates. * The unit of OBJs must be in mm. ※Recommended: * Please maintain the number of vertices of an OBJ below 1000 to avoid speed issues. * The distance between an OBJ and the ground should be 0. (You can adjust the distance in Marvelousdesigner. Button Property Setting ▶ Thread Length (cm)) #### Register Button OBJ 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. → Register Button window appears. 2. After setting the following options, Click OK. Name | Set the name of the button file. ---|--- Thumbnail | Apply the thumbnail of the button file. Button (ver. 11) | Set the properties for the button file to be registered. ※Note: If the OBJ shape is different for each button size, click the + button on the top right to register as buttons of various sizes. Size Name | Set the size name. OBJ | Load the OBJ file to be registered with the button. Width/Thickness/Weight | Set the width/thickness/weight of the button. Default Size | Set the size to be applied by default when changing with the button. → The registered button is saved in the path below. ▶ Assets ▶ Materials ▶ Hardware_and_Trims ▶ Button & Buttonhole ▶ Button #### Create Button OBJ by Thread Type 1. Set the Mesh name of the button to REN_BUTTON, REN_THREAD. 2. Create an OBJ for each thread type with the above MESH name. Set the name of the OBJ file for each thread type to *_Cross.obj, *_Parallel.obj , *_Square.obj. 3. Register the created OBJ file as a button. 4. Save the created *_Cross.btn, *_Parallel.btn , *_Square.btn files in the path below. C:\Users\Public\Documents\Marvelousdesigner\Assets\Materials\Hardware_and_Trims\Button & Buttonhole\Button 5. Run Marvelousdesigner and change the type of the thread in the button property window > Type > Thread Type.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for registering custom OBJ files as buttons in Marvelous Designer, detailing necessary requirements, recommended practices, and step-by-step instructions for successful integration.

title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Open/Save Fabric
content: Save a commonly used fabric as a PSP file and reload it to use as needed. At Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Fabric, press Save to save and press Open to load the saved Fabric data.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for saving and reloading commonly used fabrics as PSP files using the Fabric Property Editor in Object Browser.

title: Delete Buttonhole Style
content: ### Objective Delete unnecessary buttonhole styles. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab 2. Select a buttonhole style to be deleted. 3. Press the Delete key on keyboard or right click on the buttonhole style and select Delete. → The selected buttonhole style is deleted.
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for deleting unnecessary buttonhole styles in the Object Browser's Buttonhole Tab.

title: Merge
content: ### Objective Merge two Patterns in to a single Pattern. ### Location #### Pattern Outline Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern #### Sewing Line Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Edit Sewing 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Sewing ### Operation #### Pattern Outline 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern 2. Select two Pattern outlines which two Patterns are to be merged accordingly. ※ Note: When the Patterns are symmetrically linked, select the Pattern outline of the either Pattern. 3. Right click on the selected Pattern outlines to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Merge. → The selected two Patterns are merged based on the selected Pattern outlines. → The original Pattern outlines are changed to Baselines. #### Sewing Line 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Edit Sewing 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Sewing 2. Right click on the Sewing Line which the Patterns are merged accordingly. Then, select Merge. → The two Patterns sewn with the selected Sewing Line are merged based on the selected Sewing Line. → The original Pattern outlines are changed to Baselines.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for merging two pattern outlines and their associated sewing lines into a single cohesive pattern.

title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Adjust Collision Thickness
content: ### Objective Simulation thickness is invisible set property that represents the collision limit for Garments to result smooth Simulation. By default, the Simulation thickness from the Garment Pattern is set 1.5mm on each side, for a total of 3mm, and this value is adjustable as required. Lower the thickness value to work on Garments that are more likely to be form-fitting, or increase the thickness value to use as padding and etc. ※ Note: For the same reason, the default value of Avatar thickness (Skin Offset) is set for 3mm. For form-fitting Garments or accurate fitting measurement, it is recommended that Skin Offset is adjusted alongside the Simulation thickness. ### Location Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ Add'l Thickness-Collision ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ Add'l Thickness-Collision 2. Enter desired rendering thickness value. →The thickness is now being adjusted and applied.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on adjusting the simulation thickness for garment patterns to optimize collision limits for smoother simulations in fashion design.
